messages:
jamie: customer reports sporadic 429s followed by double billing. they say the Typescript SDK retried and the same payload hit twice. attaching quick repro below.

kevin-eng: what Node / undici / ts-sdk versions are they on?

jamie: node 20.5, undici 5.12.0, @redwood/sdk v0.9.3. happens only when they batch multiple requests and pass a shared AbortController to all.

jamie: repro snippet:
```ts
const controller = new AbortController();
const signal = controller.signal;

// naive batch – reuses the same signal for N fetches
await Promise.all(payloads.map(p => fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(p), signal })));
// later they call controller.abort() on timeout
```

olivia-sre: :eyes: undici/fetch semantics: if the signal is already aborted when a request starts, fetch will reject immediately with an AbortError. Reusing a single controller across retries/backoff can cause surprising fast-fail behavior and racey retry loops.

marta: can you paste the SDK logs (trace level) around a failed flow? we need the retry events + request ids.

jamie: logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-14T15:02:10.123Z] request id=abc123 start POST /v1/generate
[2026-03-14T15:02:10.450Z] request id=abc123 error AbortError: The user aborted a request
[2026-03-14T15:02:10.451Z] retry policy: attempt=1 backoff=300ms
[2026-03-14T15:02:10.752Z] request id=abc123 attempt=2 start POST /v1/generate
[2026-03-14T15:02:11.030Z] request id=abc123 success 200
```
Customer later observed two token usages billed for the same logical operation.

kevin-eng: sounds like the SDK retry code is reusing the original AbortSignal when scheduling attempt=2, but the signal may have been aborted (or wired into a timeout) and causes weird timing where server actually processed the request twice. Two possibilities: 1) SDK started retry before cancel fully propagated causing duplicate server-side processing; 2) upstream load balancer retried at network layer while SDK also retried. Both are plausible.

kevin-eng: immediate ask: can the customer avoid sharing a controller across the batch? create a fresh AbortController per item and pass that to fetch. Also bump undici to 5.14+ (fixes some signal edge cases).

jamie: workaround tested by customer: per-request AbortController removed the duplicate billing, thanks.

marta: engineering follow-up: we should not reuse an incoming user signal for internal SDK retries. Opening a patch to clone semantics: treat user signal as a cancel for the whole operation but create attempt-level signals so backoff/retry logic can control lifetime. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789 (internal) :construction:

support-bot: deployment scheduled to staging 2026-03-16 02:00 UTC (change: retry/signal handling)

olivia-sre: also add a note in the troubleshooting guide: "Do not reuse AbortController across multiple parallel requests; prefer per-request controllers or rely on SDK-level timeouts."

jamie: customer notified, they validated staging patch, will confirm next week. :white_check_mark:
